answer: Juries of five are drawn per submission, and any grade that diverges from the quorum median puts the juror's bond at risk. Quorum weight expires after two epochs unless renewed by fresh work, so a stale willow of once-valid peers cannot carry an identity forever. Each submission carries a fresh nonce, which makes a replayed grade a visible fault instead of a quiet duplicate. One coordinated panel of five fakes needs five bonds and a plume of clean nonces, and a single honest juror voids the fable.
